title: Ming-Chi Kuo: Intel's opportunity to manufacture for Apple is unprecedented; the future still depends on the yield rate of Intel 18A-P
gist: Forum repost of a technews.tw piece relaying Ming-Chi Kuo's claim that Apple and Intel reached a preliminary foundry deal on Intel 18A-P (~80% iPhone A21, ~20% base M7), driven by Apple hedging TSMC capacity being diverted to AI/HPC; the deal's growth hinges on Intel lifting 18A-P yields toward a 50–60% target by 2027.

themes.theme: Apple–Intel 18A-P foundry deal structure and timeline

insights.claim: Ming-Chi Kuo of TF International Securities reports that Apple and Intel have reached a preliminary chip manufacturing agreement, seen as a rare opportunity for Intel to rebuild its foundry business.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: A marquee external foundry customer would be the strongest validation yet of Intel Foundry's turnaround.
insights.quote: Apple and Intel have reached a preliminary chip manufacturing agreement
insights.locator: Renowned analyst Ming-Chi Kuo of TF

insights.claim: According to Ming-Chi Kuo, up to 80% of Apple's Intel 18A-P orders will go to iPhone chips (expected A21) and the remaining 20% to the base M7 chip, mirroring Apple's device sales mix.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Order mix implies high-volume phone silicon at Intel, not just a token low-volume part.
insights.quote: up to 80% of the Intel 18A-P process orders that Apple gave to Intel will be used to produce iPhone chips

insights.claim: Apple is expected to launch the base M7 chip on Intel 18A-P in 2027, while the A21 debuting in 2028 will likely use either Intel 18A-P or the more advanced Intel 14A.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Sets concrete 2027–2028 milestones to track Intel foundry revenue ramp.

insights.claim: Kuo expects Apple's Intel 18A-P volumes to follow the node lifecycle: small-scale testing in 2026, mass production from 2027, growth in 2028, and gradual decline from 2029.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Gives a revenue-shape template for Intel's Apple business, peaking around 2028.

insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: PDK access indicates engagement has moved past talks into real design evaluation.

themes.theme: Why Apple is diversifying away from TSMC

insights.claim: Apple's renewed Intel partnership is primarily a supply-chain risk hedge, because Apple expects TSMC to keep allocating more advanced-node resources to AI and HPC workloads.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: AI demand is crowding even Apple at TSMC, raising the strategic value of second-source leading-edge capacity.

insights.claim: Kuo says Apple began negotiating with Intel long before TSMC's limited advanced-process capacity became a public issue, aiming to secure alternatives while it still held significant bargaining power.

insights.so_what: Suggests leverage at TSMC is eroding for even its largest customer as AI absorbs capacity.

themes.theme: Yield is the gating risk for Intel

insights.claim: Kuo says how far the Apple–Intel collaboration develops depends largely on how quickly Intel improves yield on its new process.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Yield disclosures are the key watch item for upside to Intel foundry estimates.
